title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 203 (When principal may revoke agent’s authority)

content.overview: The principal may, save as is otherwise provided by the last preceding section, revoke the authority given to his agent at any time before the authority has been exercised so as to bind the principal.
content.glance: Subject to s. 202, principal may revoke authority at any time before it has been exercised so as to bind the principal.
content.study: The principal may, save as is otherwise provided by the last preceding section (s. 202 — agency coupled with interest), revoke the authority given to his agent at any time before the authority has been exercised so as to bind the principal. Read with ss. 204–208 on partial exercise, compensation, notice and when termination takes effect.

sections.heading: Subject to s. 202
sections.body: Power of revocation is subject to section 202 (agent’s interest in subject-matter).

sections.heading: Before exercise binding principal
sections.body: Revocation at any time before the authority has been exercised so as to bind the principal.

provisions.title: When principal may revoke agent’s authority

examples.title: Application of Section 203
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 203 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 203?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 203. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 203
distinctions.body: Section 203 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 203 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Check s. 202 interest; if none, revoke before exercise that binds the principal; then apply ss. 204–208 consequences.
